artworks.title: Achilles Killing Penthesilea (Penthesilea Painter kylix)
artworks.description: Munich kylix tondo: Achilles drives his spear into the falling Amazon — the Aethiopis duel that later tradition said left him stricken with love.

artworks.title: Achilles and Penthesilea
artworks.description: Tischbein stages the aftermath: Achilles supports the dying Amazon — recognition arriving a breath too late.

artworks.title: Eos Lifting the Body of Memnon (Douris kylix)
artworks.description: Louvre G 115: winged Eos gathers Memnon's corpse after Achilles' kill — the Aethiopis as a mother's recovery of Ethiopia's champion.

artworks.title: Hydria with the Fight of Achilles and Memnon
artworks.description: Walters hydria: Achilles and Memnon duel while Thetis and Eos look on — Troy's two greatest living heroes before either falls.

artworks.title: Penthesilea
artworks.description: Michelena's Amazon queen armed for Troy — the sovereign warrior who will die under Achilles' spear in the lost epic after Hector.

popCulture.title: Aethiopis
popCulture.description: The lost epic after the Iliad — Penthesilea, Memnon, and Achilles' death at the Scaean Gate.

popCulture.title: Achilles
popCulture.description: The Aethiopis is where the invulnerable hero finally falls — Paris and Apollo ending what Hector could not.
